item.title: Critical swim speed (CSS): what it is, how it is measured and where it stops being valid
item.description: CSS is the slope between distance and time across several trials. What reviews say about protocols, why the result depends on the method and which checks to run on the data.

item.title: Swimming: how intensity is distributed and what studies say about methods
item.description: Polarized, threshold, pyramidal, HIIT, dryland strength and tapering in swimming: what was studied, in whom, and what cannot be concluded for an amateur.

item.title: Open water: safety, cold water and wetsuits
item.description: What RNLI recommends, what a review says about wetsuits and what is left to check for your area.

item.title: Swimming: race pacing and the swim leg in triathlon
item.description: What a pool pacing review and a review of swim intensity in triathlon say: what was studied, in whom, and what does not transfer.

item.title: Races and formats: open water swimming, triathlon, IRONMAN and HYROX
item.description: Distances and formats as stated by the official bodies: World Aquatics open water, World Triathlon, IRONMAN and HYROX. Distinct disciplines, no invented calendars.

item.title: Swim technique: what studies measure (stroke rate and stroke length)
item.description: Stroke rate, stroke length and arm coordination are the most studied measures. What is known, what is not, and why we publish no target values.

item.title: Cycling to train for a marathon: what transfers and what doesn't
item.description: Riding builds the aerobic engine with less impact, but it doesn't replace running. How to use it in each phase of marathon training.

item.title: Caffeine and performance: doses, timing and when to avoid it
item.description: 3–6 mg per kg about an hour before: one of the most studied aids for endurance. How to use it without upsetting your stomach or sleep.

item.title: Carbon-plate running shoes: what the studies say
item.description: How much plated shoes with advanced foam save, who gains most, how long they last and what is known about injuries.

item.title: How many carbs per hour in a marathon

item.title: FTP and power zones: what they measure and how far to trust them
item.description: FTP is a practical estimate of threshold, not threshold itself. How to run the test, how to use the zones and when to check them again.

item.title: Polarised or pyramidal: how much intensity you really need
item.description: The best endurance athletes spend most of their time at low intensity. How to spread easy, moderate and hard work across your week.

item.title: Sleep and recovery: the cheapest performance gain
item.description: Short sleep hurts performance, mood and recovery. How much to sleep, why sleep extension works and what to do when your schedule doesn't help.

item.title: Strength for runners and cyclists: interference or advantage?
